# gm design directions

This note turns the evidence in `research/deep-research.md` into design directions. Each direction is marked as confirmed by the evidence, or as a hypothesis gm must test on its own workload before it becomes a design rule.

## jayzee-20 friction, 2026-11-04

Source: peer session jayzee-20 (run 2026-11-04-16-36-00-a12151), section "gm (this session)" of /workspace/game-6/.jayzee/reference/LESSONS.md. Each item: hypothesis, then live witness before and after the change.

- Item 1, slash-command args truncated. Not changed; the host side is not verified here. Hypothesis: the host splits the slash-command arguments on whitespace and gives the one declared argument only its first word. Witness: this run's task is "make" for a prompt that has more words. The server keeps the whole argument: native/components/mcp/tests/mcp_test.cpp:567 asserts prompts/get keeps the whole task, and the Node commit gate (src/gate.mjs:210-215) checks the same and passed on both commits below. The argument description (native/components/mcp/server.cpp:1911) already says some hosts pass only the first word.

- Item 2, background output dropped. Changed: 0cc8958d0e6511711fae8fd4b813be25e8a42675 (src/runcode.mjs). Hypothesis: a stopped background body (finish with stopBackground) replies only "the body stopped before it returned", so its return value and console output are lost without a statement. Witness before, node harness on runBody, stopped after 2.6 s: {"ok":false,"error":"the body stopped before it returned"}. After: "the body stopped before it returned: its return value and console output are lost; 6 verb calls completed before the stop, each in query_log as a code-call after seq 1". A body that completes after its budget still returns its full value through job_status (body-900 returned {"names":4,"ok":4,"fail":0,"parts":["step 0",...]}). The 120 s move to background was not reproduced: a 130 s body with timeoutMs 280000 returned in the foreground (elapsedMs 130001). The live stop path needs finish, which this child does not send, so the witness is the node harness.

- Item 3, gm.grep hides untracked files. Changed in the Item 3 change line below. The live grep is native/components/search/search_impl.cpp (footer at line 520, skip hints appended after it), and native/ belongs to gmc. Witness before: "(0 matches; showing 0 to 0; no more)" then "hint: 1316 files skipped (5 untracked, 1311 gitignored or in node_modules); use scope: 'all' to include them". An edit of src/search.mjs that moved the hints first left the live output unchanged, so it was reverted. Fix for the native owner: emit the skipped-count hint before the footer. scope all finds the untracked probe file (jayzee20-leak-probe.txt:1), so the data is reachable.

- Item 3 change, commit 270639743b55ba83ac2773bc846fcd075212d522 (native/components/search/search_impl.cpp, search.cpp, tests/search_test.cpp, AGENTS.md). Hypothesis: the default scope reads only the git ls-files tracked paths, so an untracked file that git does not ignore is never searched, and the skipped hint comes after the footer. Refuting witness: after the change, a probe that is untracked and not ignored is not found by default. Witness before, live gm.grep with default arguments (run 2026-11-04-07-53-54-3c7bb2, actionSeq 1189): "(0 matches; showing 0 to 0; no more)" then "hint: 1316 files skipped (5 untracked, 1311 gitignored or in node_modules)". Witness after, the built binary over stdio (build/release/native/components/host/gm serve, run 2026-11-04-17-42-32-927f11): the untracked probe is found by default as ".grep-untracked-probe.tmp:2"; a gitignored probe is not found by default and the reply begins "hint: 1402 files skipped (17 in node_modules or vendor, 1385 gitignored)"; scope all finds the gitignored probe as "build/grep-ignored-probe.tmp:1". Build: cmake --build build/release, all 63 targets; ctest in build/release, 13 of 13 passed. src/search.mjs, the Node reference, keeps the tracked-only default and is not changed here.

- Item 4, body load error had no location. Changed: 691fa75e9893a09970293683894740552c5f0468 (src/runcode.mjs, src/body-worker.mjs). Hypothesis: Node's ESM SyntaxError carries no file line in its message or stack, so the location comes from node --check. Witness before: "the body does not load: Unexpected identifier 'jayzee'". After: "the body does not load: Unexpected identifier 'jayzee' (line 2, column 19)" for the statement on body line 2, and "(line 3, column 19)" for the same statement after an import line that is removed from the code. The lesson's "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" example does not fail to load: it runs and fails with "PIPESTATUS is not defined". A backtick inside a template literal ends it early and produces the reported message.

- Item 5, refusal does not name next_context. Not changed; already correct. src/mcp.mjs:600-601 and native/components/mcp/server.cpp:923-924 both name next_context ("call next_context to open a new run", and for a child "the session that opened it calls next_context to open the next run"). native/components/mcp/tests/mcp_test.cpp:284 asserts the text. Not reproduced live, since that needs finish.

Not in the five items:
- gm.grep accepts a file as root (commit 6d708a2, search.cpp): one tracked file, or any file with scope all; path cannot be combined with it. gm.search still refuses a file root ("refused: root is not a directory").
- The live server is mixed: run_code bodies run from src/ and pick up edits at once, while grep and the MCP surface are native. A fix in src/ may not reach a verb served natively.
- Four untracked work/rows/unknown-*.yml files in the shared checkout belong to another session and were left alone.

## Hot reload language (2026-11-04)

Owner direction, 2026-11-04: choose the ideal language for hot reload. QuickJS is not mandatory, and every option is a candidate. Decision: hot code is ES2023 JavaScript run by QuickJS-NG, in one fresh context per leaf call. This supersedes decisions 4 and 7 of "Rewrite on deoxidene" for the leaves: the leaves are JavaScript modules in native/leaves/, not native plugins in native/plugins/.

Candidates, judged on reload cost, crash isolation, toolchain needed at edit time, portability to the six targets, and one language with run_code bodies:

| Option | Reload cost | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native C++ plugin, rebuilt on change and loaded with dlopen (deoxidene tier 0, spike in docs/spikes/hmr) | A compile per edit, then a load. A loaded DLL cannot be overwritten on Windows, so each load needs a copied file. A crash in a plugin takes the worker down. | Rejected for leaves. Every machine that edits gm would need a C++ toolchain at edit time. Core code stays native and restarts through the relay instead of reloading. |
| QuickJS-NG, leaves as JavaScript modules, fresh context per call (chosen) | No compile step. A changed file is read and its bytecode cached by mtime; the next call uses it. Deoxidene measured about 0.1 ms per runtime and context. | Chosen. One language for leaves and run_code bodies, C source with no dependency, builds with any C compiler on the six targets, and an exception stays inside its call. |
| Lua 5.4 or LuaJIT | As QuickJS | Rejected: run_code bodies are JavaScript, so Lua would be a second language for the leaves. |
| Hermes | As QuickJS | Rejected: a much larger source tree and build for the same job. |
| WebAssembly modules (wasm3 or WAMR as the interpreter) | A compile to wasm per edit | Rejected: needs a compiler at edit time, as native does, plus an extra runtime. |
| Node.js as the host (gm today) | An ESM loader hook, cheap | Rejected for the rewrite: it keeps the Node runtime the rewrite removes. It stays the live runtime until cutover. |
| Embedded Python | Interpreter reload | Rejected: a heavy runtime and a third language. |

Rules that follow from the choice:
- A leaf is native/leaves/<name>.mjs. It exports verbs, an array of objects with name, description, inputSchema and call(args). A leaf keeps no state at module level, because each call runs in a fresh context.
- A leaf reaches the host only through host.<name>(args), where the name is a native verb (read_file, write_file, list_dir, stat_file, edit_file, search, grep, and the others) or one of the extra primitives (run, shell, logAppend). It uses no Node or engine-specific API, so the same file also runs under node in its tests.
- Reload: a call recompiles a leaf when its mtime or size changes. A file that does not compile keeps its last good bytecode, and the error goes to the caller and the log, as the Node loader keeps old code on a refused reload.
- The core (MCP server, run log, job table, verb table, primitives) is C++. A change to it restarts the worker through the relay, as today.
- Witness: an edit to a leaf takes effect on the next call with no restart. The latency is measured and recorded here.

## Rewrite on deoxidene (2026-11-04)

Owner direction, 2026-11-04 (`/mcp__gm__gm`): rewrite gm starting from `../deoxidene` as the boilerplate, keep gm's hot reload, and the orchestrating session decides the rest. Decided by the orchestrator under that delegation:

1. Language and build: C++23 with deoxidene's CMake presets, library headers (`include/deoxidene/`), vendored `third_party/tl/` and CTest setup. Preset names are the ones in `CMakePresets.json` (x64 and arm64 on Linux, Windows and macOS). Built and tested here with GCC 15.2, CMake 4.2, Ninja.
2. Node stays the live runtime until the native build reaches parity and is witnessed. `src/` and `tools/` are not edited during the port: a half-made edit there is live to every running worker (see AGENTS.md, "shared checkout is live"). Cutover is one commit that points `.mcp.json` at the native binary, and it needs a reconnect.
3. `run_code` bodies run in QuickJS-NG (deoxidene tier 1, measured in the QuickJS spike of deoxidene (its docs/spikes/quickjs)). The `gm.*` verbs are bound as native functions, so bodies stay JavaScript and existing prompts and skills keep working.
4. Hot reload: superseded by "Hot reload language (2026-11-04)".
5. `fetch` runs the system `curl` (present on macOS, Linux and Windows 10 and later), so there is no TLS library. No new library was added.
6. `callers` and `impact` (code-ast) need a JavaScript parser. acorn is pure JavaScript, so it is vendored as a file and run inside QuickJS-NG; no native parser is written.
7. Layout: `native/components/<name>` holds the core (json, log, host, quickjs, mcp, verbs, relay), and `native/plugins/<name>` holds the leaf plugins. `native/CMakeLists.txt` adds every directory that has a `CMakeLists.txt`, so a directory is added only once it configures and builds.
8. Comments: the new code has none. A reason that cannot be read from the code goes to AGENTS.md after it is checked (INVARIANT 6).
9. Commits are attributed to lanmower with no trailers and pushed to origin main at each witnessed milestone. Nothing is pushed that breaks the running gm.

Milestones: M0 the scaffold configures and its boilerplate tests pass. M1 json and the run log pass their tests. M2 the native binary serves the three-tool surface over stdio from a fresh run. M3 each verb group matches the JavaScript on the same inputs. M4 a plugin edit is live in the running process, shown by a new generation. M5 cutover.


## Finish waits for every row (2026-11-04)

Friction from oscraft: runs ended with rows open. Run 2026-11-04-07-24-35-be3eb8 ended at seq 6007 with 34 PRD rows open, recorded as gaps. Run 2026-11-04-14-27-00-a85d22 ended at seq 29 with its open rows listed as gaps (prd-mw1bzqqz7f60, prd-liveswapverify2setup). Cause: finish took `stopRows: true`, which ended the run with each open row listed as a gap, and skill step 6 named it as the way past open rows.

Rule (owner direction, 2026-11-04, from deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype docs/003-execution.md): a ticket ends only when no work remains open. A ticket that needs a person waits in a person stage and resumes on the person's reply. Closing one artefact does not end the ticket while work is unfinished.

Decision:
- `stopRows` is removed from finish (src/mcp.mjs) and from its description. finish is refused while any PRD or unknown row is open, and the refusal names the rows.
- A gap that names an open row id is refused: "gap names open row <id>; a gap cannot stand in for an open row".
- A question for the owner is an open unknown row (`gm.unknown_add`). It keeps the run open until `gm.unknown_resolve` records the answer.
- Only `gm.prd_delete` drops a row. Checked: prd_delete refuses an unknown row and a resolved PRD, and unknown_resolve refuses a commit that is not in the repository and an event that is not in the run's log. Both match skills/gm/SKILL.md step 6.
- skills/gm/SKILL.md step 6 and AGENTS.md (Surface, Rows) no longer name stopRows. README.md did not name it.

Changed: prd_add and unknown_add log a row-added event (fields row, rowKind, title) through host.logAppend, and row-added is a pending kind in native/components/mcp/pending.cpp and src/pending.mjs, so events --wait wakes when a PRD or question row is added. The owner's reply to a question still reaches the session as a message; the wait is started again after the answer.
Also: unknown_resolve needs a commit that exists. An answer that changes no file has no commit of its own, so its witness is an existing commit, for example HEAD.

Impact at the change: src/mcp.mjs is in src/worker-modules.json, so the change restarted each worker on the checkout. The live workers before it were gm pid 1087915 (open run 2026-11-04-07-53-54-3c7bb2), oscraft pid 2457829 (its last run 2026-11-04-14-27-00-a85d22 had ended) and gmc pid 2529361 (open run 2529320-17406516). No job or background body was running: each run's jobs directory held only exited or killed jobs, and no action was in flight after the last restart of an open run.

Witness, on a scratch copy of the tree under /tmp/gm-scratch/gm/finish-stop, through the MCP entry (node src/mcp.mjs over stdio, playwriter disabled with --mcp-config):
- Before, unchanged code, run 2026-11-04-14-58-01-13734a: seq 11 refusal "refused: 1 row(s) open: prd-mw28r5o6e8e3 witness row. Work them, or finish with stopRows: true to end with them listed as gaps". finish with stopRows true returned {"ok":true,"finished":true}, and seq 16 end {"status":"finished","gaps":["open row prd-mw28r5o6e8e3: witness row"]}.
- After, run 2026-11-04-14-58-32-c4ba7b: seq 11 and seq 13 refuse with "refused: 1 row(s) open: prd-mw28rtlu8146 witness row. Resolve each with its witness, or delete a PRD you will not implement with prd_delete. A question for the owner stays open until the owner answers" (stopRows true is refused the same way). Seq 15 refuses "refused: gap names open row prd-mw28rtlu8146; a gap cannot stand in for an open row, so resolve it or, for a PRD, delete it". gm.prd_delete returned "prd-mw28rtlu8146 deleted", and seq 25 end {"status":"finished","witness":"witness probe: row deleted by prd_delete, no open rows remain"} with no gaps.
- Question row, run 2026-11-04-14-58-49-68f62e in a git scratch workspace: unknown_add gave unknown-mw28s6t530fe, and seq 11 refusal names it. unknown_resolve was refused for commit deadbeefdeadbeef ("no commit deadbeefdeadbeef in this repository") and for event 99999 ("event 99999 is not in this run's log"). prd_delete was refused ("id must name a prd row, with an id that starts prd-"). unknown_resolve with commit 1f19c8fc8ad6 returned "unknown-mw28s6t530fe resolved by event 1 at commit 1f19c8fc8ad6", and seq 33 end finished.
- On the edited checkout itself, the same two scenarios: run 2026-11-04-14-59-38-146a42 gave refusals at seq 11, 13 and 15 and end at seq 25; run 2026-11-04-14-59-38-37844b gave refusal at seq 11 and end at seq 33.

## History squash (2026-11-04)

The Rust port and its removal are out of gm's history, because the rust/ blobs made every clone larger. Commits up to and including `c9172c4` keep their shas. From `19b14bd` on, every commit has a new sha, and `a360041` was dropped because it touched only rust/. The tree at HEAD is the same as before the squash (`2618522e`). Old to new: `19b14bd` to `6adfc95`, `4e9fa56` to `b937311`, `56e0586` to `d23e974`, `84f508a` to `247cee0`, `9b7ba65` to `ae4d5a5`, `bac1557` to `1161f49`, `5035c17` to `9140693`, `584f50d` to `b67df48`, `82a8104` to `e61140e`. Backup bundle of the pre-squash history: /config/gm-pre-squash-2026-11-04-b.bundle (outside the repo; the first backup is /config/gm-pre-squash-2026-11-04.bundle).

## Decided

Superseded: earlier conformance counts and row ids in this section are historical; native conformance is 63 checks in 23 scenarios.

- Scope: a fresh worker that replaces gm's loop, not a fork of gm. Reason: one worker, one log and one loop is the simplest design the evidence supports.
- Language: Node.js 22 or later, ES modules (see "Node floor 22 (2026-11-03)" at the end of this file). Dependencies: one pinned runtime dependency, acorn 8.18.0. No native code and no submodules. Any further dependency needs a measured gain in turns or accuracy, and a measured memory cost per worker, recorded here first. Decided 2026-11-02 as the joint decision of the owner and the orchestrator, which replaced the zero-dependency rule; see "Dependency rule, joint decision" below. The orchestrator rejected the agent's earlier change, which had added thorns and node:sqlite and raised Node to 22.5, and that change is reverted by the commit that records this rule. Reason: acorn is small and has no native code, and it gives exact call sites, which cuts the turns spent verifying callers and impact.
- Shape: gm is an MCP server (stdio, JSON-RPC written by hand with Node built-ins, no network listener) plus a skill at `skills/gm/SKILL.md`. The Claude Code session is the model. The CLI is a thin wrapper for scripted witnesses. Reason: owner decision, relayed by the gm agent (2026-11-01). It supersedes the earlier single-CLI shape, because the host model is already the worker.
- Self-iteration: gm runs on itself. The project .mcp.json starts tools/supervise.mjs with --runs runs/self and task tasks/self.md. Each server start gets its own run directory under runs/self. A run resumes only with an explicit --resume <run-id>. finish closes only that run, and a later session starts a new one. The skill and the self-task say the same. The step budget is 100000, which is correct for a shared project run. The gm agent decided this on the user's instruction (2026-11-01). The user approves the server once, in /mcp, the first time Claude Code opens the project, and nothing in gm can grant that. ccbridge sessions do not read project .mcp.json. gm writes nothing into any host's global config. The project .mcp.json is the only registration, and it lives in the repo.
- Hot reload: tools/relay.mjs holds the host connection and runs tools/supervise.mjs, which runs the worker as a child (see the relay bullet below). A change under src/ or skills/ holds new host requests, waits for calls in flight, pauses the worker with SIGTERM, starts a new one on the same run, and resumes the run from its log. A call still running is never interrupted or answered with an error: the restart waits until its result is logged. Background jobs stop at a restart, and each stop is logged. A broken source is reported, and the next good change recovers. It registers nothing in any config. Reason: the user asked for hot reload while the worker runs.
- Hot reload, decided and witnessed (gm agent, 2026-11-01): the project .mcp.json runs the host-facing relay, which runs the supervisor and the worker, so a running session reloads on a source change.
